activity_summary: On the way to church you passed the Guild Chapel and the bolted door of the school. Hamnet said they could walk past it on a Sunday without their Latin. You told Susanna you had known the Latin best when Ovid had a story in it, and you sent them on past the school stair.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Answered Susanna about the Latin, and sent them on past the stair.

entities.name: Edmund Shakespeare
entities.context: Named tomorrow morning's lesson, and was told off the mounting-block.

entities.name: Hamnet Shakespeare
entities.context: Named the bolted door, and the white wall of the chapel.

entities.name: Susanna Shakespeare
entities.context: Asked whether he had known the lesson before the bell stopped.

entities.name: Anne Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked with them, and did not take the talk.

entities.name: Mary Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked with them. The mounting-block was left because she would have said so.

entities.name: Joan Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked with them, and kept Judith in the line.

entities.name: Richard Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked with them, and said nothing.

entities.name: Judith Shakespeare
entities.context: Walked in the line, and said nothing.

facets.activity: Walked past the closed school door

quotes.speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
quotes.text: The schoolhouse door is bolted with the great staple on a Sunday, Edmund.

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: I knew the Latin when Ovid had a story in it, Susanna, and the master knew the birch when he had not.
